materials.title: What Enters a Cup
materials.text:
A college tasting club compared tea prepared from the same batch of dried ____1____. The plant material was placed in water, but the resulting drink was not simply the original material in a smaller shape. Some substances could ____2____, entering the water at a molecular level, while many solid pieces remained visible.

The club called the prepared drink an ____3____ because water had stood in contact with the plant material to extract soluble substances. To remove floating pieces before tasting, the students poured it through a ____4____. This step separated larger solids; it did not necessarily remove the substances already present in solution.

They kept the water ____5____ the same across samples, measuring how hot it was when each preparation began. They also recorded the ____6____ of water in each cup, since adding the same amount of leaf material to different quantities of water could produce different results. The time in contact with water was the variable they deliberately changed.

A stronger ____7____ meant that more of the relevant dissolved material was present per unit of drink. It did not mean that every flavour became more pleasant. A long steep could taste ____8____, with an unpleasant sharp quality for some participants. Individual preference was recorded separately from preparation time.

The students described the smell rising from each cup as its ____9____. Solid material remaining after pouring was the ____10____. They kept smell, taste and leftover solids as separate observations. Their small comparison could describe these particular preparations, but it could not establish one perfect brewing time for every tea, cup or drinker.

questions.explanation: C leaves：dried修饰复数植物材料，leaves茶叶；residue是倒出后的残留物，非起始批次。

materials.title: A Size Number Was Not Enough
materials.text:
A walking club invited a shoe fitter to a preparation meeting. Several members assumed that the printed size alone would establish comfort. The fitter measured each foot's ____1____ from back to front, then checked its ____2____ from side to side. Two feet with a similar first measurement could still require differently shaped shoes.

The back part of the foot was the ____3____. It needed to remain reasonably secure rather than rise excessively with every step. The fitter adjusted the ____4____, the cords threaded through the upper part of the shoe, to alter how it held the foot. Pulling harder was not always better: a shoe that became too ____5____ could squeeze the wearer.

The bottom part contacting the ground was the ____6____. For the intended walk, it needed to bend appropriately rather than behave like an entirely stiff board. A suitably ____7____ material could accommodate that movement. This did not establish that the softest possible shoe was suitable for every surface.

The group also discussed ____8____, rubbing between surfaces that could irritate skin during repeated steps. Concentrated ____9____ meant force acting over a limited area, another possible source of discomfort. These mechanisms were related but were not identical descriptions.

A small fluid-filled skin injury caused by repeated rubbing was a ____10____. Members were advised to stop and seek suitable help if discomfort developed, rather than treat pain as proof that a shoe was becoming effective. The meeting was about checking fit before the walk; it did not provide a diagnosis or claim that one shoe design could prevent every foot problem.

questions.prompt: A Size Number Was Not Enough: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: J length：back to front为长度；width侧到侧下空，cushioning缓冲性质不属于前后尺寸。

questions.prompt: A Size Number Was Not Enough: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.

questions.explanation: F laces：cords threaded through鞋带，复数对应they隐含多根；pattern图案不是可拉紧绳。

questions.prompt: A Size Number Was Not Enough: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: A tight：squeeze穿者表示过紧；waterproof防水、flexible柔韧均不直接表达挤压合脚问题。

questions.prompt: A Size Number Was Not Enough: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: G sole：bottom contacting ground为鞋底；heel指已述脚跟，不概括整个鞋底部件。

questions.explanation: L blister：fluid-filled skin injury明确水疱；repair修理行为、pattern图样均非皮肤损伤。

materials.title: Visits between Blossoms
materials.text:
An orchard class watched bees moving among apple flowers. The bright outer flower parts were ____1____. Their colour, together with the flower's ____2____, could contribute to attracting visitors. The class kept visual appearance separate from the smell perceived near the blossoms.

Bees collected ____3____, a sugary liquid, as one food resource. Fine grains of ____4____ could also attach to their bodies. These grains had a role in plant reproduction and were not another name for the sweet liquid. A visit could therefore involve food collection while also moving reproductive material.

The receiving flower part was the ____5____. When suitable pollen reached it, the movement was described as ____6____. This event did not itself guarantee that every flower would eventually develop into a mature apple. Later conditions and processes still mattered.

Researchers could ____7____ pollen deliberately between flowers in a controlled comparison. They covered some blossoms to reduce visits by ____8____, the animal group that includes bees. The coverings were part of an experiment, not an assertion that all plants relied on bees or that no other movement of pollen was possible.

An apple was the eventual ____9____ considered in this example, while the observation period was ____10____ because flowering occurred during a particular part of the year. The class recorded flower visits and later development separately. Counting one bee landing was not the same as counting one apple produced. This distinction helped pupils ask what their observation actually measured before drawing conclusions about the orchard's harvest.

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: G petals：bright outer flower parts为花瓣；roots根在地下，stigma是后述特定受粉部位。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: N scent：与visual separate及smell对应气味；nectar液体、pollen颗粒不是气味属性。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: A nectar：sugary liquid明确花蜜；pollen是颗粒，下句显式区分。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: C pollen：fine grains reproductive material为花粉；nectar花蜜非颗粒。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: E stigma：receiving flower part为柱头；petals吸引作用与该部位不同，hive蜂巢不属花部。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: I pollination：花粉到接受部位的转移为授粉；fruit是后续果实，不是转移事件。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: K transfer：could后原形，between flowers移动花粉为transfer；wind作为风名词不命名此有意操作。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: L insects：bees所属动物类昆虫，复数在visits by后；roots植物器官，hive栖居处非动物类。

questions.prompt: Visits between Blossoms: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: F fruit：apple是本例果实；ripe成熟形容词不能在the eventual后作此名词分类。

questions.explanation: O seasonal：particular part of year说明季节性；sterile不育与观察时段性质不同，ripe修饰果实而非观察期。

materials.title: Meeting the Platform
materials.text:
A rail museum used a stationary ____1____ to explain boarding arrangements. The vehicle did not move during the demonstration. Visitors compared its floor with the platform, noticing that two different dimensions could cause difficulty.

The ____2____ distance was the separation across from platform edge to vehicle doorway. The ____3____ difference concerned how far one surface stood above the other. Reducing one did not automatically remove the other. A narrow space could still include a significant step.

Where both surfaces were at the same height, the guide described them as ____4____. A remaining ____5____ could still lie between them. A short flat board could ____6____ that space under the museum's controlled demonstration, forming a connection rather than changing the height of the whole platform.

A sloping ____7____ could accommodate a height change. Its ____8____ described the steepness of the slope, so the distance available for the slope mattered. The demonstration did not suggest that every steep board was an appropriate boarding aid.

The staff used a ____9____ device that could be carried into position and removed after use. Correct ____10____ meant that its relevant edges and the doorway were placed in the intended relation. The guide checked this before anyone used the model.

The exhibit distinguished a building feature, a vehicle position and a movable aid. It did not offer instructions for independent use on an active railway. Its purpose was to show why calling a station accessible required more information than saying that one step had been removed. Conditions at the actual door and platform mattered together.

questions.prompt: Meeting the Platform: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: H carriage：stationary vehicle为车厢，可数a后；barrier隔栏不是供上车的车辆。

questions.explanation: A horizontal：across from edge to doorway说明水平距离；vertical垂直高度在下空。

questions.prompt: Meeting the Platform: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: F gap：remaining separation空隙；gradient坡度不是两物间空位。

questions.prompt: Meeting the Platform: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: C bridge：could后原形动词，bridge that space跨接间隙；announce宣布、signal发信号不构成连接。

questions.prompt: Meeting the Platform: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: I ramp：sloping board适应高差为斜坡道；barrier挡板功能相反。

questions.explanation: B gradient：steepness of slope为坡度；alignment对齐关系不是坡的陡度。

materials.title: Absence from a Notebook
materials.text:
A conservation seminar examined repeated surveys of ponds for an amphibian. The relevant ____1____ was the wetland environment used by the species. Whether a site was actually occupied during the defined study period was its ____2____ state. The observation process was a separate matter: a present animal could remain unnoticed.

The probability of recording the species when it was present concerned ____3____. Search duration, weather and observer experience could affect that process. The team recorded survey ____4____ as time spent searching, rather than assuming every visit represented the same opportunity to notice an animal.

A written ____5____ specified how each visit should be conducted. Following it improved comparability, although it could not make imperfect observation disappear. Additional visits provided temporal ____6____, repeated observations of the same site within the period for which the occupancy state was assumed stable. The team explicitly considered whether that stability assumption was defensible.

Measured features used to explain variation were ____7____ in the statistical model. Some described sites; others described visits. Treating them as interchangeable would confuse ecological conditions with observation conditions. The model combined these components to ____8____ the probability that sites were occupied, rather than simply equating an empty notebook with an empty pond.

Conclusions remained ____9____ where observations were limited or the assumptions were weak. The investigators reported that uncertainty rather than rounding every result to certainty. A claim of local ____10____, the disappearance of the species from a site, would require more justification than one unsuccessful search.

The exercise did not assert that repeated visits inevitably identified every hidden state. It showed why absence of a record and absence of an organism were different propositions. Assumptions about changes during the study and relationships among visits had to be evaluated alongside the numerical output.

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: A habitat：物种使用的环境为habitat；migration迁移过程不指环境。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: B occupancy：地点在期内被占据的隐藏状态；abundance数量不同，detection记录过程被后文区分。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: E detection：存在条件下被记录概率属检出；occupancy存在本身，不是观察是否成功。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: H effort：time spent searching定义调查努力量；protocol方法规范不是实际搜索时长。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: F protocol：written specifications为规程；likelihood似然函数不规定现场方法。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: C replicates：additional visits repeated observations为重复观测，复数；covariates解释特征并非再访问。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: M covariates：measured explanatory features为协变量；replicates是重复观测单位，abundance是数量状态。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: J estimate：to后原形，对概率作统计估计；migration名词不能作此动词，likelihood亦名词。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: L uncertain：limited evidence/weak assumptions使结论不确定；independent是独立性，seasonal是季节性，均不回应证据不足。

questions.prompt: Absence from a Notebook: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: D extinction：disappearance from site为本地灭绝；migration迁移不保证局地永久消失，abundance仅数量。

units.title: 六级选词：时间银行中的记账与责任

materials.title: An Hour Recorded Twice
materials.text:
A neighbourhood time bank allowed members to provide approved services and earn credits measured in hours. The arrangement encouraged ____1____, a pattern of mutual giving and receiving, without requiring the person who received one service to repay the same provider directly. It was distinct from an ordinary cash ____2____ for employment: the scheme's credits did not claim to settle every legal question about work.

When a member completed an accepted task, the recorded service was a ____3____ to the scheme. A coordinator checked that both parties agreed the task had occurred. An entry became ____4____ after that confirmation, rather than merely because one participant had submitted a request.

Transactions were kept in a ____5____, a chronological accounting record. A member's available ____6____ reflected credits earned and used under the local rules. Recording the same task twice would distort that amount even if the duplicated descriptions were individually plausible.

Using earned credits to receive a service was ____7____. The scheme's ability to meet such requests depended on willing members and suitable skills; a positive account did not guarantee immediate access to every kind of assistance. The coordinators therefore distinguished a record from a promise of unlimited supply.

The rules defined ____8____, the conditions under which a person could join and participate. They also specified an ____9____ date after which unused credits would no longer remain valid. That condition was explained before members joined, rather than introduced after their contributions.

If participants disagreed about a recorded task, a ____10____ could be submitted for review. The review considered the evidence and the announced rules; it did not assume that the larger recorded balance necessarily belonged to the more truthful person. The seminar used the example to separate social purpose, accounting events and obligations. Calling the arrangement mutual aid did not remove the need to explain what each account entry meant.

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: B reciprocity：mutual giving/receiving定义互惠规范；O overdraft透支是可用额度不足的账户状态，本段没有负余额机制；其他候选分别命名工资、贡献、核实、账簿等不同事件或属性。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: E wage：cash payment for employment为工资；liability负债义务非工资支付类别，balance账户净额非雇佣支付。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: K contribution：completed accepted service为贡献；redemption是后述使用积分，不是赚取服务。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: H verified：after confirmation为核实状态；anonymous匿名不由双方同意推出，transferable可转让也非认证。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: F ledger：chronological accounting record为分类记账簿；balance余额为其中计算值，非记录载体。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: I balance：earned and used后可用净额为余额；inflation物价上涨不是成员账户数。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: A redemption：using earned credits兑取服务为兑换；contribution提供服务方向相反。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: G eligibility：conditions to join为资格；liability责任与加入条件不同，exchange交易不命名资格。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: N expiry：date after which invalid为到期；dispute争议非期限，inflation非日期规则。

questions.prompt: An Hour Recorded Twice: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: M dispute：disagreed case submitted review为争议；ledger记录本身、wage工资均非双方异议案件。

units.title: 六级选词：统计表中的抑制与反推
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: A Blank Cell Still Revealed
materials.text:
A statistics office prepared a table showing counts of service users across small districts. Several cells contained very few people. Publishing an exact count beside a distinctive category could make information about an individual easier to discover, so the underlying records were treated as ____1____ rather than open for unrestricted inspection.

The office's rule used a ____2____, a numerical cutoff below which a cell required additional protection. Removing the displayed value was ____3____. Yet hiding a single cell did not necessarily protect it: row and column ____4____ could allow a reader to subtract all visible counts and recover the missing one.

The analyst therefore considered ____5____ protection, withholding further cells so that the first hidden value could not be obtained by that simple subtraction. This was a coordinated treatment of the table, not an assertion that every unprinted number was equally sensitive.

Another approach used ____6____, reporting counts to a stated numerical interval rather than retaining all their digits. A different technique deliberately added controlled changes, or ____7____, to the published values. These methods affected what readers could calculate, and their properties depended on the specified procedure.

The agency assessed ____8____, the usefulness of the published table for its intended analyses, alongside disclosure risk. Combining categories through ____9____ could reduce detail, but it might also conceal differences important to users. A larger table was therefore not automatically more informative for every purpose.

Before public ____10____, the office tested whether protected values could still be derived from combinations of totals and earlier publications. It documented the transformations and limitations. The exercise showed that a visible blank was a presentation feature, whereas protection concerned what could be learned from the entire information environment. No single visual treatment guaranteed that all routes to identification had disappeared.

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: C confidential：records restricted from open inspection为保密的；reversible可逆、complementary互补不表访问属性。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: J threshold：numerical cutoff为阈值；denominator分母非任意保护界限，precision精度非门槛数。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: B suppression：removing displayed value为抑制发布；rounding取整、perturbation扰动都仍可显示修改值。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: L margins：row/column totals为边际合计；denominator是比率分母，本段没有比率计算。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: H complementary：further cells protect initial suppression为互补抑制；reversible可逆反而非此额外保护角色。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: F rounding：report to numerical interval为舍入；aggregation合并类别，perturbation刻意加变更不同机制。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: N perturbation：controlled deliberate changes为扰动；suppression不发布值，rounding按固定间隔约化，不等本段另述加变更。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: M utility：usefulness for analyses为效用；precision仅数字精细度，不概括用途适配。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: A aggregation：combining categories为聚合；inference推断是读者得结论，不是合并数据分组操作。

questions.prompt: A Blank Cell Still Revealed: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: G release：before public后名词，公开发布为release；consent同意非发布事件，inference推理不是机构公开动作。

units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: Reading across Witnesses
materials.text:
A seminar prepared a critical edition of a short historical poem surviving in several handwritten copies. The copies were textual ____1____: material sources that preserved forms of the work, not necessarily independent testimonies to its original wording.
